methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series C → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.7x) to $380M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
ZeroAvia is a Series C–stage transportation company that has raised $380M+ to date. The frontier-tech transportation sector comprises eight private comparables, including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Slate Auto, and Harbinger; no public peers provide direct valuation benchmarks.

A single triangulation method applies here. Stage-progression analysis uses the $380M cumulative raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement, yielding $646M. Peer-median valuation was not applicable: while three same-sector peers exist in the data, none satisfied minimum thresholds for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or valuation-tier clustering required to produce a reliable median—fewer than three datapoints in any filtered bucket would introduce material selection bias.

The analysis supports a median valuation of $646M, with a plausible range of $549M (low) to $743M (high) reflecting reasonable variance around the stage-progression central estimate. Key uncertainties include the absence of a calibrated peer median—critical for confirming whether ZeroAvia's position within the transportation frontier-tech landscape is consistent with its stage and capital deployment—and reliance on raised capital as a proxy for current value, which does not account for burn rate, technical progress milestones, or market conditions since the most recent financing.
